verdict.reasoning: The patient confirms, “It's been happening for about three days now” in reference to his diarrhea; the note also opens with ‘you're suffering from bad diarrhea.’
Patient states, “It's been happening for about three days now,” referring to the diarrhea.
When asked how many times a day, patient replies, “Four to five.”
The clinician asks if it is watery or loose; patient says, “It probably depends on the time of day, to be honest,” implying variable consistency over time.
Patient describes “pretty standard diarrhea where there's like a little bit of abdominal pain,” which indicates mild abdominal pain.
Patient explicitly says, “I threw up once.”
In response to fever questions, patient says, “Maybe a little bit, but it hasn't been that in particular hasn't been too worrying,” consistent with a possible low‑grade fever.
Patient notes, “A little bit of appetite loss, I guess, versus the normal.”
When asked about drinking, patient confirms, “Yeah, yeah, yeah,” and clinician summarizes, “you're still drinking plenty.”
Despite symptoms, the patient reports only “a little bit of appetite loss” and confirms ongoing drinking, indicating some oral intake is maintained.
When asked, “Is there any blood…?” patient responds, “No blood.”
After mucus is explained, patient answers, “No, no,” indicating no mucus.
Patient says, “no travels recently,” when discussing past episodes and current context.
Patient notes, “nothing funky in my diet,” indicating no clear dietary trigger.
Patient states, “I. Probably at asthma or. Or, I don't know, I guess I still have it,” confirming a history of asthma.
Patient indicates the asthma persists (“I guess I still have it”), consistent with a chronic condition; no other acute qualification is given.
When asked if using any inhalers, patient answers “Yes” and provides a name, indicating active inhaler use.
Patient repeatedly says “Lexapro?” / “Lexipro?” as the inhaler name during the medication discussion.
The transcript notes inhaler use but does not state any explicit plan such as ‘continue current inhaler as usual’ or comment on changes vs no changes.
When asked about allergies, patient replies, “Nothing. Yeah, nothing. … No allergies at all.”
Patient says, “My dad had hypertension… Has hypertension? … Hypertension. Yeah.”
Patient states, “He died of bowel cancer 10 years ago,” and when asked age, replies, “62.”
Clinician comments, “you look like you're not dehydrated, which is a good sign,” indicating visual assessment of no dehydration.
While the exact term “gastroenteritis” is not used, the entire encounter and advice clearly interpret this as an acute diarrheal illness of a few days’ duration.

All components are documented: 3 days (“about three days now”), 4–5 stools/day (“Four to five”), variable loose/watery consistency by time of day, one vomiting episode (“I threw up once”), maintained intake (still drinking; only mild appetite loss), and no blood or mucus (“No blood… No, no” for mucus).

Asthma is mentioned and inhaler use confirmed, but the assessment section in the transcript does not explicitly restate asthma as a chronic condition in the assessment nor link it to a management plan.
Clinician stresses hydration: “You still need to drink plenty of water because you're losing a lot of fluids,” which is oral rehydration advice.
Clinician says, “you could get something called Di Rolite over the counter. So it helps to replenish the salts…” which is an oral rehydration powder recommendation.
Clinician advises, “a soft diet… that will be like crackers, toast, jam, those kind of things that's easily digestive.”
Advice includes, “avoid dairy… while you're having the diarrhea” and “Milk is not a good idea.”
Clinician says to “avoid… meat… while you're having the diarrhea” and not to “have meat immediately once you feel like you're slightly better.”
Clinician advises avoiding “eggs while you're having the diarrhea.”
Clinician states, “although you can't. Milk is not a good idea. Yogurts are a good idea because they are probiotics.”

Clinician explains to resume meat/eggs/fish after 48 hours diarrhea‑free: “Once you're okay with [mash vegetables] for about 48 hours, then you can start having meat… You'Re not having any diarrhea, you're fine, then you can go and start having meat, egg, fish.”
There is no mention of antidiarrheal antibiotics at all, nor an explicit statement that no medications were started; only Di Rolite and diet advice are discussed.

Clinician states concern thresholds: “When we start worrying about diarrhea is if you're going more than eight times a day…” and later, “if you're going about six to eight times a day… you might need to go into hospital… If that happens, do get in touch with us again,” which is safety‑net advice tied to stool frequency and dehydration risk.
Clinician advises, “if your diarrhea doesn't go away in a week's time… We need a stool sample,” prompting further care if >1 week.
Clinician says, “if you're passing blood. We need a stool sample,” i.e., seek further assessment if blood in stools.

While dehydration risk and possible need for hospital are mentioned with high stool frequency, there is no explicit broad advice about ‘signs of dehydration or worsening symptoms’ as a separate criterion beyond frequency and duration; stool sample is tied to blood or 1‑week persistence, not explicitly to dehydration signs.
No explicit asthma management plan is discussed; asthma or inhaler regimen is not addressed in the plan section.
Clinician says, “If that happens, do get in touch with us again,” referring to high stool frequency and potential dehydration, which is re‑contact advice when safety‑net criteria are met.
Clinician notes, “All this is all recorded in your app, so you can go back… you can go back and read the notes,” indicating follow‑up information in the app.
